01

January 2027

Leuven University, Belgium · 4 hours of training

Course leaders

Andy Temmerman

Wim Teughels

Webinar

Between modules, a live webinar with the module’s course leader.

Learning objectives

  • Understand the biology of bone healing after tooth extraction and its influence on the alveolar process.
  • Understand osseointegration and the influence of surface topography, implant design and osteotomy site preparation.
  • Know the biological differences between teeth and oral implants at macroscopic, microscopic and histological level, and their influence on surgical procedures.
  • Review important anatomical features in oral surgery and implant dentistry.

02

February 2027

Academy for Oral Implantology, Vienna, Austria · 4 hours of training

Course leaders

Robert Haas

Lukas Fürhauser

Georg Mailath Pokorny

Georg Mailath Pokorny Jr.

Sebastian Pohl

Rudolf Fürhauser

Webinar

Between modules, a live webinar with the module’s course leader.

Learning objectives

  • Know which clinical diagnosis is appropriate for each patient’s situation.
  • Learn key points of treatment planning for optimal aesthetic results.
  • Know the fundamentals of radiology.
  • Read 2D and 3D X-rays correctly and avoid misinterpretations.

03

March 2027

University Egas Moniz, Lisbon, Portugal · 4 hours of training

Course leaders

Gil Alcoforado

Ricardo Alves

Webinar

Between modules, a live webinar with the module’s course leader.

Learning objectives

  • Understand implant types (bone and tissue level), connections, macro and microgeometry.
  • Understand surgical instruments and pre- and post-operative care.
  • Incisions and flap design according to local anatomy.
  • Understand the basic principles of correct 3D implant placement and surgical protocols according to implant type and bone density.
  • Suture materials, and second stage surgery to enhance soft tissue quality and quantity.

04

April 2027

University of Geneva, Switzerland · 4 hours of training

Course leaders

Irena Sailer

Vincent Fehmer

João Pitta

Webinar

Between modules, a live webinar with the module’s course leader.

Learning objectives

  • Select the best type of restoration and material for each patient situation.
  • Know new CAD/CAM materials, their indications and limitations.
  • Apply the digital workflow to single and multiple implant restorations.
  • Understand the titanium-based concept in everyday clinical practice and the differences between screw-retained and cement-retained restorations.

05

May 2027

University of Zurich, Switzerland · 4 hours of training

Course leaders

Ronald Jung

Webinar

Between modules, a live webinar with the module’s course leader.

Learning objectives

  • Understand the possibilities and limitations of alveolar ridge preservation.
  • Make the right decision in each individual clinical situation.
  • Choose the right materials for alveolar ridge preservation.
  • Know when to use an autogenous graft and when to use an artificial soft-tissue substitute.

06

June 2027

University Complutense, Madrid, Spain · 4 hours of training

Course leaders

Eduardo Montero Solis

Eduardo Cárdenas

Ana Carrillo de Albornoz

Ignacio Sánchez

Webinar

Between modules, a live webinar with the module’s course leader.

Learning objectives

  • Diagnose and treat established peri-implant diseases.
  • Manage mechanical complications.
  • Implement preventive strategies to maintain peri-implant health and the integrity of the implant reconstruction.

FAQ

Questions before you book?

Everything you need to know about the format, schedule, exams and subtitles.

Implant dentists and general practitioners who want the essential knowledge and confidence to deliver predictable implant treatment.

Entirely online: six modules and 24 hours of training, from January to June. Between modules, a live webinar with the module’s course leader.

Each module is released on a specific date according to a predefined schedule. The full programme calendar will be shared with participants before the start of the course. Once a module is released, its videos can be watched at any time while the platform remains open.

Modules remain accessible until the platform closes. Participants can therefore complete them at their own pace during the period of access.

A complete schedule, including the platform access period and closing date, will be shared with participants before the start of the programme.

No. Live webinars are optional and are not required to complete the programme. However, they will not be recorded and can only be attended live.

An exam is available at the end of each module. You can take them as you go, or all of them at the end of the programme.

Participants must complete all module examinations and achieve a score of 100% in each exam. Each exam can be retaken as many times as necessary. Once all exams have been successfully completed with a score of 100%, the Certificate will be available for download directly from the platform.

Chinese, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish and Turkish.

The First Certificate covers fundamental principles. The Second Certificate covers more advanced clinical topics. The First Certificate starts in January and the Second Certificate in June. EAO members can book both together at a reduced price.
